title.en: A woodblock behind Hiroshige’s fish prints
title.zh: 广重鱼类版画背后的木版

alt.en: A dark rectangular wooden printing block bears carved outlines of two fish, blossoms and rows of Japanese writing.
alt.zh: 深色长方形印刷木版上，刻着两条鱼、花朵与成行日文。

caption.en: Japan, c. 1840–1842. Woodblock for Utagawa Hiroshige’s design of olive halibut, black rockfish and cherry blossom, from the so-called Large Fish series.
caption.zh: 日本，约1840—1842年。用于歌川广重所谓《大鱼》系列中牙鲆、黑鲉与樱花图案的印刷木版。

interpretation.en: Carved fins, scales and lettering reveal the skilled work behind reproducible pictures. This surviving block is a tool used to make paper impressions. The museum credits Hiroshige with the design; its carver and printer remain unidentified.
interpretation.zh: 雕刻的鱼鳍、鳞片与文字展示可复制图像背后的技艺。这块留存木版是制作纸本印张的工具。馆方将图案归于广重，刻工与印工的身份未详。

ledger.visualReview: Full 1200 × 830 image inspected: dark wooden block, two opposing fish, individually cut fins and scales, blossoms, Japanese text; chipped/worn edge and lower-right labels. This is a physical printing block, not an imagined historical likeness. Selected first media FS-8002_12; second media has inconsistent dimensions and is not admitted.

relationship.en: Fine carved fins, scales and lettering reveal the skilled work behind the woodblock prints named in the Edo urban-culture entry. This is a printing tool, not a finished paper impression: it makes the material process behind reproducible pictures visible. The museum attributes the design to Hiroshige but does not identify a block carver or printer; the designer should not be assumed to have performed every production step.
relationship.zh: 精细雕刻的鱼鳍、鳞片与文字，展示江户城市文化条目所述木版画背后的技艺。这是印刷工具，而非完成的纸本印张，使可复制图像背后的物质工序可见。馆方将图案归于广重，但未指明刻工或印工；不能假定设计者亲自完成所有制作步骤。

title.en: Edo Japan: cities under warrior government
title.zh: 江户日本：武家政权下的城市

summary.en: Under Tokugawa rule, artisans and merchants contributed to a vibrant urban culture despite their lower place in the official social hierarchy. Kabuki theatre, woodblock prints and popular literature served expanding city audiences. Older courtly and Chinese-inspired traditions were also reworked rather than simply abandoned. Foreign contact was controlled, with limited exchange continuing through places such as Nagasaki; Japan was not entirely sealed off. Edo’s cultural history therefore connects state regulation with commercial creativity. The contrast between official status and economic influence is a useful way to explore how social orders actually functioned.
summary.zh: 德川统治下，工匠与商人虽在官方等级中地位较低，却推动了城市文化。歌舞伎、木版画和通俗文学面向不断扩大的市民群体，旧有宫廷传统和中国风格也被重新诠释。对外交往受到限制，但长崎等地仍有交流，日本并非完全封闭。江户文化显示国家规范与商业创造如何并存，也揭示法定身份与经济影响力的差距。

dateNote.en: Uses the source’s 1615–1868 art-historical focus, not the 1603 establishment date of the Tokugawa shogunate.
dateNote.zh: 采用来源的1615—1868年艺术史关注时段，并非德川幕府1603年建立日期。
